# Section 13: Financial and Physical Resources

Section 13 addresses financial stability, budgeting, and physical infrastructure.

## Standard 13.1 — Financial Resources [CR] {.core-requirement}

::: {.callout-important}
## Core Requirement
:::

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

The institution has sound financial resources and demonstrates financial stability.

### Typical Evidence Types

- Audited financial statements (3 years)
- Budget documents
- Fund balance/reserve policies
- Financial trend analysis
- Debt service coverage

### Suggested Owners

- Chief Financial Officer
- President
- Board Finance Committee

### Common Pitfalls / Weak Evidence

- Declining fund balances without explanation
- Audit findings not addressed
- Unrealistic budget assumptions
- Missing financial documentation

::: {.callout-note title="NC Considerations"}
NC community colleges receive funding through:

- State appropriations (FTE-based formula)
- County appropriations (capital and operational support)
- Tuition and fees
- Grants and contracts

Document relationship with county funding and state allocation processes.
:::

---

## Standard 13.2 — Financial Documents [CR] {.core-requirement}

::: {.callout-important}
## Core Requirement
:::

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

The institution has an annual independent audit and addresses any findings.

### Typical Evidence Types

- Annual audit reports (3 years minimum)
- Management letters
- Responses to findings
- Evidence of corrective actions

### Common Pitfalls / Weak Evidence

- Repeat audit findings
- Findings not addressed
- Late audit completion

---

## Standard 13.3 — Financial Responsibility

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

The institution exercises appropriate financial controls and oversight.

### Typical Evidence Types

- Internal control documentation
- Budget monitoring procedures
- Purchasing policies
- Financial reports to board

---

## Standard 13.4 — Control of Finances

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

The institution exercises proper control over all financial resources.

### Typical Evidence Types

- Policies for all fund types
- Foundation relationship agreements
- Auxiliary enterprise oversight
- Grant management procedures

---

## Standard 13.5 — Control of Sponsored Research

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

If conducting sponsored research, appropriate oversight exists.

### Typical Evidence Types

- Grant management policies
- Compliance procedures
- Financial oversight of grants

*Note: Many community colleges have limited sponsored research. Document what exists or state that the standard has limited applicability.*

---

## Standard 13.6 — Federal/State Responsibilities

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

The institution is in compliance with federal and state requirements related to financial responsibility.

### Typical Evidence Types

- Title IV compliance documentation
- Default rates
- Financial responsibility composite score
- Program review results

::: {.callout-note title="NC Considerations"}
NC community colleges must comply with both federal Title IV requirements and NC state financial policies including:

- SBCC fiscal policies
- NC Office of State Budget and Management requirements
- Local Government Commission oversight (for borrowing)
:::

---

## Standard 13.7 — Physical Resources

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

The institution provides adequate physical resources for its programs and services.

### Typical Evidence Types

- Facilities master plan
- Space utilization data
- Maintenance and renovation budgets
- Safety and security documentation
- ADA compliance

### Suggested Owners

- Facilities Director
- Chief Financial Officer

### Common Pitfalls / Weak Evidence

- Deferred maintenance backlog
- Safety issues not addressed
- No facilities master plan

---

## Standard 13.8 — Institutional Environment

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

The institution provides a healthy, safe, and secure environment.

### Typical Evidence Types

- Safety policies and procedures
- Emergency management plan
- Campus security reports (Clery Act)
- Health and safety inspections

---

## Reflective Prompts

- What is the institution's financial trajectory?
- How are audit findings tracked and addressed?
- What is the status of deferred maintenance?
